title: Schrödinger and Dirac Dynamics over Finite Holographic Substrate
content: We derive the operational content of the Schrödinger--Dirac formalism on a finite holographic substrate: a totality whose capacity---the de Sitter entropy \(S\)---bounds the state count of every embedded observer. The totality is a timeless torsor, and an observer is a prime shell \(\mathbb{F}_p\), nested in it, whose clock is the drive of its frame. The Lorentzian form depends on its temporal coefficient only through the square class, and the drive multiplier is the canonical coefficient. Over the quadratic extension, Hamiltonians are self-adjoint and their Cayley steps unitary, and the Cayley map identifies the self-adjoint projective line with the norm-one cycle \(C_{p+1}\), the boost group that transports the Dirac operator. The Dirac operator factors into a spinorial Klein--Gordon operator, and a spinor form forced by the arithmetic makes its evolution unitary, with massless periods a power of \(p\) and mass phases on \(C_{p+1}\). The free evolution is the drive itself, with its spectrum on the drive cycle \(C_{p-1}\), and the drive cycle and the norm-one cycle meet in \(\{\pm 1\}\) alone: the two wave equations are the two Fourier pairs of one shell. Transports are reversible, and power maps lose \(\log \gcd(\varepsilon, p - 1)\) of Hartley entropy. Every identity is formalised in \textbf{Lean}; the continuum enters only as a labelled reading.
